html:
Homo naledi is an extinct species of human found in 2013 deep in the Rising Star cave system near Johannesburg, South Africa, in the area known as the Cradle of Humankind. The bones date to between about 335,000 and 236,000 years ago.

Cavers exploring Rising Star found bones in a chamber reached only through a very tight chute. The palaeoanthropologist Lee Berger recruited a team of slim scientists who could squeeze through. They recovered more than 1,500 pieces of bone from at least fifteen individuals.

The species is a puzzle. Its brain was small, less than half the size of ours, and its shoulders and fingers suited climbing. Yet its hands and feet were much like ours.

Berger's team argues that Homo naledi deliberately placed its dead in the cave, and perhaps made marks on its walls. Many other scientists doubt this. Either way, several kinds of human lived in Africa alongside early Homo sapiens. Compare the small Homo floresiensis of Indonesia, and the far older Taung Child found in South Africa in 1924.
